newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - 18 February 1997.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - 18 February 1997.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

-- ENGLAND STAR IN DRUG ROW Member of the England cricket team Phil Tufnell has been thrown out of a New Zealand restaurant following staff allegations that they had discovered him smoking marjuana in a disabled person's lavatory. After the Middlesex bowler strenuously denied the allegations, England cricket chiefs leapt to his defence.
-- BRITANNIC GIVES DIVI A 902 MILLION LIFT

As Britannic Assurance becomes the latest life insurance and pension provider to benefit from the distribution of an orphan asset investment surplus, shareholders in the company are set to receive an 82 percent increased dividend.
-- FLAGGING YEN BOOSTS JAPAN TRADE SURPLUS

The Bank of Japan today stated that it would continue to watch the effect that exchange rates have on domestic prices. Currently the weaker yen continues to boost Japan's trade surplus, helping to slow the pace of growth in imports.
-- GULF SET FOR CLYDE VICTORY BY A WHISKER
The highly competitive bid for Clyde Petroleum the North Sea oil producer reaches its conclusion today. The 496mn stg bid by Gulf Canada is expected to be successful.
Profits at Coal and Allied, RTZ-CRA's Australian coal subsidiary dived by 99.3 percent last year which has prompted new speculation that the company will be sold. -- BMC +44 171 377 1742
